messages.content: my plan says if my brother comes, i will make tea. i made tea. can you know he came?
not from that rule alone. you might make tea for another reason too. the rule says what happens if he comes, not that he is the only reason for tea.
what if i say i only make tea when he comes, and i kept that rule today?
then yes, if you really kept the rule that tea is made only when he comes.
make that answer shorter.
yes, if you kept that new rule today.
what changed between my first idea and my new rule?
the first left other reasons for tea open. the new rule says no tea without him coming.
make that explanation shorter.
the new rule makes his coming the only reason for tea.
only give the answer for my first rule again.
no. making tea does not tell us for sure that your brother came.
write a longer story about a child finding a plan for the afternoon and asking whether it is still the plan. make the question useful for what he does next.

a child found a page on the table saying that the family would visit the park after lunch. he began putting his book away, then saw another page under it about reading with his grandmother. he asked his mother which plan was for today. she explained that the park page was from another day and had been left there. today, they were reading at home before dinner. he put the old page with other used paper and brought his book to the right room. his question had taken only a moment, but it kept him from getting ready for a journey nobody else was making. later, his mother asked him to help move the paper so the new plan would be the one easy to find.
why did he ask instead of using the first page he saw?
there were two pages with different plans, and he did not know which was for today.
what was the plan for today?
reading with his grandmother at home before dinner.
did asking mean he chose not to help?
no. he checked so he could get ready for the right task.
make that explanation shorter.
asking helped him choose the right task.
finish with the reading place ready.
he brought the book, moved a chair near his grandmother, and opened the first page.
four friends were going to come. all but one came. how many came?
three came. one did not come.
does but mean the same thing there as in i wanted to go but i stayed home?
all but one says everyone came apart from one person. in the other sentence, but makes a difference clear between what you wanted and what happened.
make that explanation shorter.
all but one is about a group with one left out. the other but makes two different ideas clear.
use examples instead of that explanation.
all but one friend came. i wanted to go, but i stayed home.
only give the part about the different choices.
i wanted to go, but i stayed home.
only give the number from the first question again.
three.
i read a story again after a long time. the words are the same, but i care about a different person now.
a different part may be important to you now, even while the words stay the same.
make that reply shorter.
the same story can have a different part you care about now.
i used to follow the child most. now i keep thinking about the mother.
that gives you a different question to bring to the same story.
can you help me write one sentence about it?
the story has not changed, but i am thinking more about the mother than i did before.
does that say my first reading was wrong?
no. you can care about another part now without saying the first reading was wrong.
make that explanation shorter.
a new part being important does not make your first reading wrong.
only give my sentence again.
the story has not changed, but i am thinking more about the mother than i did before.
write a longer story about two people who share a desk. one thinks a book left there says the other is still using it, so they make the plan more clear.

a brother and sister used the same desk at home. one afternoon, the sister saw his book on it and waited in another room because she thought he was still reading there. he had finished long before and was outside. when he came in, she asked how much longer he needed the desk. he said he was done, then understood why she had waited. they chose a simple plan: when finished, each would put their book away or say that the desk was free. the next day, he left a note saying the book could be moved and the desk used. she put it on the shelf and began her drawing. the book itself had not been a clear message about whether the place was still in use.
why did she wait?
she saw his book and thought he still needed the desk.
was he still using it then?
no. he had finished and gone outside.
what made the next day more clear?
a note said the book could be moved and the desk used.
can an object being left always tell you the person is still there?
no. people may leave things after they are done. more context may be needed.
finish with her putting her own things away.
when she finished drawing, she put the page with her book and told him the desk was ready for him.
what is different about take the book off the table and turn the music off?
take the book off the table is about moving it away from the table. turn the music off is about making it stop playing.
can you make one sentence with both?
please take the book off the table, then turn the music off.
does off always name a place?
no. its meaning changes with the other words, such as take off and turn off.
what if i say the radio is off?
that usually says it is not playing or working at that moment, not that it moved to another place.
make that explanation shorter.
it is about the radio not playing, not about moving it.
only give the sentence about the table again.
please take the book off the table.
write an eight word sentence about reading with my sister by the window.
i read with my sister by the window.
now add yesterday at the end. how many words will it have?
nine words.
only give that sentence.
i read with my sister by the window yesterday.
now make it a plan for tomorrow and use we instead of i.
we will read with my sister by the window tomorrow.
how many words is that?
ten words.
why did it get longer?
will was added to make the plan. we took the place of i, and tomorrow took the place of yesterday.
only give the first eight word sentence again.
i read with my sister by the window.
my friend is reading a page. i need to know when they will finish, but do not say they are slow.
you could ask: about how much time do you need to finish the page?
can i say why? i need the book next.
about how much time do you need to finish the page? i would like to use the book after you.
what if they do not know yet?
then they can say that, and you can choose whether to wait or use another book if you have one.
can i ask to be told when it is ready instead?
yes. please let me know when you are finished with the book is a clear request.
make it a question.
could you let me know when you are finished with the book?
why not say you should have finished already?
because you have not given a time they said they would be finished. you only need information about when the book will be ready.
make that explanation shorter.
ask about the time you need instead of adding a fact you do not know.
is i have gave her the note right?
use i have given her the note. given goes with have in that sentence.
can i use gave without have?
yes. i gave her the note yesterday is correct.
now make a question with did.
did you give her the note yesterday?
why give after did?
did goes with give in that question. gave is used without did in the sentence about yesterday.
what if i want a request for tomorrow?
please give her the note tomorrow.
can you know who her is from only that sentence?
no. her needs context to tell us which person you mean.
only give the sentence with have again.
i have given her the note.
write a longer story about a child asked to move a book. he thinks that he must stop reading, but the other person only needs a little space for a cup.

a child was reading at the table when his brother asked whether the book could be moved. the child closed it and began putting it away, thinking the reading time was over. his brother explained that he only wanted a little space for a cup. the book could stay on the table if it moved to one side. they opened it again and found enough room for both things. after that, the child asked what kind of move was needed before closing the book. his brother also said the small change he wanted more clearly. neither had needed the whole table, and the reading could go on.
what did the brother need?
a little space for a cup.
why did the child first put the book away?
he thought moving the book was a request to stop reading.
what could he ask before closing it?
do you need a little space, or do you need the whole table?
make that question shorter.
how much space do you need?
finish with the table still useful to both.
they kept the drawing and book on one side and found enough room for the cup on the other.
that example helped with one sentence. i still need to learn the rest, but do not give me more now.
okay. we can stop with the part that helped.
can you say something kind without saying i know everything now?
you have one more part that is clear than before.
make that sentence more simple.
one more part is clear to you now.
only say goodbye next.
goodbye.
the cup was on the desk this morning. now it is on the shelf. was my first sentence wrong?
not if it really was on the desk this morning. a new place now does not change where it was before.
can you put both facts in one sentence?
the cup was on the desk this morning, but now it is on the shelf.
why but instead of and?
but makes the change stand out. and can also give both facts, without making the difference as clear.
make that explanation shorter.
but makes the change more clear. and simply gives both facts.
now only use and.
the cup was on the desk this morning, and now it is on the shelf.
can you know who moved it?
no. you gave the two places, but not the person who moved the cup.
